walkthroughs.h2: c = f × λ for EM waves
walkthroughs.body_html:
Every EM wave obeys c = f × λ, where c = 3 × 10⁸ m/s.

So if you know the frequency, you can work out the wavelength — and vice versa.

Example: visible light at f = 6 × 10¹⁴ Hz has λ = c / f = (3 × 10⁸) / (6 × 10¹⁴) = 5 × 10⁻⁷ m. That's green light. 💚

Because c is fixed, frequency and wavelength are inversely linked. If one goes up, the other must go down.

Radio: long wavelength, low frequency.
Gamma: short wavelength, very high frequency.

So if you're told a wave has the highest frequency in the spectrum, you instantly know it has the shortest wavelength too.

Use standard form when numbers get scary. 3 × 10⁸ means 300,000,000. 10⁻⁷ means 0.0000001.

When you divide, subtract the powers. (3 × 10⁸) ÷ (6 × 10¹⁴) = 0.5 × 10⁻⁶ = 5 × 10⁻⁷.

Always include units: wavelength in m, frequency in Hz, speed in m/s. ✅

mcqs.q: All EM waves travel at the same speed when they are in what?
options: Water
Glass
A vacuum
Air at sea level

mcqs.q: If two EM waves have the same speed but different wavelengths, what must be different?
options: Their colour, always
Their frequency
Their direction
Their amplitude

mcqs.q: If one EM wave has a higher frequency than another, what is true about its wavelength?
options: It is unchanged — only the speed differs.
They have the same wavelength because both are used for communication.
It is also longer, because both increase together.
It is shorter — wavelength and frequency are inversely related (c = f x lambda).

mcqs.q: Which has the longer wavelength: microwaves or radio waves?
options: Radio waves — they sit at the longest-wavelength end of the EM spectrum.
Microwaves, because they are used in 'big' devices like radar.
Yes — UV is the colour purple.
They have the same wavelength because both are used for communication.

mcqs.q: Is ultraviolet light visible to humans?
options: No — even though it sits next to violet on the spectrum, its frequency is above the range our eyes detect.
Yes — UV is visible because it's right next to violet.
They have the same wavelength because both are used for communication.
Yes — UV is the colour purple.
